name: Vinayak Damodar Savarkar
role: Indian revolutionary, writer and Hindu nationalist ideologue; coined Hindutva; president of the Hindu Mahasabha (1937-1943)
summary: Savarkar (1883-1966) began as an armed revolutionary against British rule, was transported to the Andamans, and after his release in 1924 became the main ideologue of Hindu nationalism, defining a Hindu as one who holds India as both fatherland and holyland and treating the Hindus as a nation. As Hindu Mahasabha president he demanded one man one vote and equal citizenship with no communal electorates, an undivided India, Hindu militarisation, a machine-age nationalist economy that co-ordinated class interests, and war on caste untouchability, cow worship and superstition in the name of science, while describing Muslims as a hostile community and urging retaliation against enemy civilians in his history.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Keer quotes his argument that nations superior in military strength survive and dominate while militarily weak ones are subjected, and that absolute non-violence is immoral; he demanded Hindu militarisation, military training in schools and an army of the Indian people (Mahasabha programme, 1948 statement).

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Keer's biography (chapter 'Hindu Manifesto or Savarkarism', summarising his presidential addresses at Ahmedabad, Nagpur, Calcutta and Madura) reports: His programme envisages a casteless Hindu society with voluntary inter-caste marriage; caste is hereditary rank, though the statement is not about caste by name.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Keer's biography (chapter 'Hindu Manifesto or Savarkarism', summarising his presidential addresses at Ahmedabad, Nagpur, Calcutta and Madura) reports: His programme says people would first of all welcome the machine age, with national production on the biggest possible machine scale and science leading all material progress.

all-land-state-owned.rationale: His Calcutta 1939 presidential address (Hindu Rashtra Darshan), his economic policy of national co-ordination of class interests: in some cases the Government may take over land and introduce State cultivation with big machines; Keer's summary of his programme goes further, saying all land would pass to the State by and by. The primary text says only some cases, so low.

armed-resistance-to-occupation.rationale: He calls the revolutionary mentality against an alien armed oppression justifiable and says he fought as a soldier for fifty years for independence (1948 written statement); Six Glorious Epochs praises armed Indian resistance to foreign invaders. His 1857 book defends armed revolt against foreign rule.

change-traditions-that-no-longer-suit.rationale: Keer says he stands for today, not the blind traditions of yesterday, and asks Hindus to test their holy books against science; he fought untouchability against orthodox custom.

character-from-environment.rationale: In My Transportation for Life he writes that there are very few races or families of hereditary criminals, that heredity and race are not yet settled scientific facts, and that the convict should normally come out a better man after reclaiming discipline and education. That puts weight on environment and training over innate nature.

civil-marriage.rationale: Keer's summary of his programme has Hindu marriage customs secularised and voluntary inter-caste marriages freely performed. Civil ceremonies are not named, so low.

civilians-legitimate-targets.rationale: In Six Glorious Epochs (the section on perverted conceptions of virtue) he criticises Shivaji and Chimaji Appa for returning captured Muslim women and argues Hindu victors should have punished enemy women in kind, by forcible conversion and absorption, so that future conquerors would fear reprisals on their women; he also calls for super-atrocious reprisals against the atrocities of aggressors. He treats enemy civilians as legitimate targets of retaliation.

class-collaboration.rationale: His Calcutta 1939 presidential address (Hindu Rashtra Darshan), his economic policy of national co-ordination of class interests: the interests of capital and labour are subordinated to the nation and their claims co-ordinated; profits shared in a flourishing industry, diminishing returns accepted by both in a losing one.

class-struggle-history.rationale: His Calcutta 1939 presidential address (Hindu Rashtra Darshan), his economic policy of national co-ordination of class interests: he rejects economic interpretation of all history as one-sided and holds that national, racial and religious differences persist despite economic community of interest.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: In 1937 he demands that Gomantak (Portuguese India), Pondicherry and other Hindu-inhabited parts be claimed as inalienable parts of the one Hindusthan, and in 1948 he states the ambition to restore the Motherland from the Indus to the Seas. These claims concern land held by other colonial powers or severed by partition rather than a claim on a neighbouring state, so low.

communal-electorates.rationale: He prefers joint electorates and one man one vote (1937, Calcutta 1939) and in 1948 recalls the Mahasabha's opposition to the Communal Award; in 1939 he adds that if the constitution is communal, minorities wanting separate electorates or reserved seats may have them in proportion to their population. His own position is against, with a pragmatic fallback, so medium.

conscription.rationale: In 1939 he calls on Hindus to compel all universities, colleges and schools to make military training compulsory for students and to secure entry for Hindu youths into the naval, air and military forces (Hindu Rashtra Darshan); Six Glorious Epochs praises ancient republics where the whole nation could be drafted. Compulsory training is close to but not the same as conscription into service, so low.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Keer quotes the Abhinav Bharat creed that sovereign power must rest in the hands of the Indian people; he also demands one man one vote in 1937. Low because the legitimacy question is not addressed directly.

country-wealth-only-from-land.rationale: Keer's summary of his programme calls the peasantry and working classes the chief source of national wealth and has national production on the biggest possible machine scale, so wealth is not tied to land alone; the claim itself is not discussed, so low.

culture-before-state.rationale: In 1937 he says the absolute political independence of Hindusthan is a sine qua non for the all-round regeneration of Hindudom, and that independence is only worth having if it also secures Hindu cultural identity; he treats the two together but makes the political state the precondition.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Keer quotes his account of the Huns and Shakas as hordes inferior to the Hindus in language, religion, philosophy and mercy though superior in strength, and his survival-of-the-fittest framing; he treats Hindu culture as superior in several respects, which rejects the claim that no culture is superior.

decide-locally.rationale: Keer's biography (chapter 'Hindu Manifesto or Savarkarism', summarising his presidential addresses at Ahmedabad, Nagpur, Calcutta and Madura) reports: He favoured a powerful centralised state of Hindusthan with residuary powers vested in the Central Government and backed the 1935 federation scheme to strengthen the Centre.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: In his Mahasabha war policy (1939-42) and his 1948 statement he urged Hindus to take part in the war efforts of industrialisation and militarisation that defended India, while pressing the British for Dominion Status as the price of sympathy; he did not call on Indians to work for the defeat of their own government. The government in question was British rule over India, so medium.

destroy-worshipped-objects.rationale: In Six Glorious Epochs he writes that a Hindu king who conquered the region of Somnath should have wiped out every mosque there, and criticises Hindus for not destroying mosques at Kashi, Mathura and Rameshwaram after defeating Muslim powers. This concerns the shrines of a faith he treats as an aggressor, not worshipped objects in general, so low.

direct-action.rationale: In 1937 he urges Hindus to vote only for candidates pledged to Hindutva and to capture whatever political power the Reforms Act gives, and his 1948 statement says the Mahasabha stood for constitutional change once the state was free; he defended revolution against alien rule but did not set direct action in place of electoral politics.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: In Hindutva he writes that to try to prevent the commingling of blood is to build on sand, that sexual attraction has proved stronger than the commands of all the prophets, and that all anyone can claim is the blood of all mankind; barriers between races are artificial.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Keer's chapter on his writings reports he holds a fundamental and natural difference between man and woman, that their duties differ and so their education should differ (a woman a ministering angel, not an Amazon), while he opposes old useless customs binding women and calls female education indispensable. This concerns education and home duties, not what the law should say about public roles, so low.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Keer quotes him that India must not lose the strength born of national and racial cohesion, and warns that Hindu-Muslim differences, which he calls two nations, threaten the Indian State; he also says no people is perfectly homogeneous and that Hindus themselves differ in language and custom. The link is implied, not stated as a general claim, so low.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Keer's biography (chapter 'Hindu Manifesto or Savarkarism', summarising his presidential addresses at Ahmedabad, Nagpur, Calcutta and Madura) reports: His programme grants fundamental freedoms to all citizens but allows restrictions in the interest of public peace and order or national emergency, on common national grounds, not religious ones.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Keer's summary of his programme says public services would go by merit alone, and in 1937 he demands no distinctions of religion or race in public services, offices or franchise and no weightage for any community; he does not address affirmative action by that name, so low.

equal-conscription.rationale: In Six Glorious Epochs he describes, with evident admiration, the ancient Punjab republics where men and women alike had to undergo military training so the whole nation could be drafted, and calls the Youdheyas a nation in arms. This is a historical description, not a policy proposal for today, so low.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: His Hindu Rashtra Darshan addresses demand one man one vote and equal rights for all citizens irrespective of caste, creed, race or religion, and call for securing to untouchables all fundamental rights every citizen enjoys in public life, including by court action; but the Mahasabha also seeks to safeguard Hindu interests against non-Hindus, so the position is qualified.

ethnic-nation.rationale: He treats the Hindus as a race and nation bound by blood, culture and history (Hindutva; 1937 address) while proposing a state of equal citizens for minorities, so he holds a nation should be mainly one ethnic group without excluding others from citizenship.

evolved-behavioural-sex-differences.rationale: Keer's chapter on his writings reports he holds a fundamental and natural difference between man and woman, that their duties differ and so their education should differ (a woman a ministering angel, not an Amazon), while he opposes old useless customs binding women and calls female education indispensable. He frames the difference as natural, not specifically evolved.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Keer's account says the truth of his rejection of absolute non-violence was shown by the measures the Indian government itself adopted in Hyderabad and Kashmir, and that he led the fight for an undivided Hindusthan; this implies approval of force to keep regions in the state but is the biographer's gloss, so low.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: His 1948 statement records that he led the movement against vivisection of the motherland and that the Mahasabha uncompromisingly refused the Cripps scheme clause allowing partition; Keer's chapter on his fight for Akhand Hindusthan covers the same. Partition under British rule was the central issue of his later politics.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Keer's chapter on his writings reports he holds a fundamental and natural difference between man and woman, that their duties differ and so their education should differ (a woman a ministering angel, not an Amazon), while he opposes old useless customs binding women and calls female education indispensable. Treating the difference as fundamental and natural rejects the view that gender is primarily social.

gradual-change.rationale: Keer's biography (chapter 'Hindu Manifesto or Savarkarism', summarising his presidential addresses at Ahmedabad, Nagpur, Calcutta and Madura) reports: He called a revolution evolution in leaps and advocated radical social change, though he also set out reforms through law.

historical-land-claim.rationale: In 1937 he grounds the Hindu claim to Hindusthan on its being the fatherland of their forefathers and their holyland, contrasting Muslims whose holyland lies outside India, yet in the same address demands a state of equal citizens with one man one vote and no special privileges for Hindus. His words point both ways on whether historical tie gives a stronger claim than present residents.

history-own-civilization.rationale: In the introduction to Six Glorious Epochs he complains that English-written histories taught in Indian schools and colleges misled students about India's past and calls refuting them a national duty, writing history from the national point of view. He does not set a school curriculum rule, so medium.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: His definition of a Hindu rests on Bharatbhoomi being both Fatherland and Holyland (pitribhumi and punyabhumi), the cradle and temple of the faith; the 1937 presidential address restates it.

humans-entitled-to-use-animals.rationale: Keer reports his view that no animal is divine and even the cow is for man, not man for the cow, and that beef may be eaten in a grave crisis.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: His Calcutta 1939 presidential address (Hindu Rashtra Darshan), his economic policy of national co-ordination of class interests: we shall first of all welcome the machine; this is a machine age, and national production will be on the biggest possible machine scale.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Keer reports his view that no form of government or political ism is absolutely good or bad under all circumstances for all peoples alike; he does not single out Western institutions or civilizations, so low.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: The JTA reported on 23 January 1948 that he welcomed the UN decision to create a Jewish state in Palestine and said all of Palestine should have been made a Jewish state. Medium because it is a news report of his statement.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: He insisted British India, with the princely states, remain one indivisible state from Kashmir to Rameshwar and Sindh to Assam and fought partition (1937 address; 1948 statement), which in effect means keeping the inherited borders; he also claimed French and Portuguese enclaves, so the link to the colonial borders as such is indirect, hence low.

language-defines-nation.rationale: In 1937 he argues that a nation does not need uniformity of language and lists country, language, culture, history and Holyland together as what marks the Hindus out, so language alone is not enough on his account.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Keer quotes him that the Vedas and Smritis are historical landmarks, not omniscient or unchangeable works, and that their laws must be tested against science; in 1937 he says the Mahasabha takes its stand on no dogma or book. He calls for a secular state with equal citizens.

limit-guns.rationale: He led the Mahasabha's campaign for repeal of the Arms Act and for licences to sell arms as in England (1948 written statement).

martyrs-honoured.rationale: In the 1937 address he honours the Hindus who went to the gallows and to the Andamans for freedom, and elsewhere in the address cites Pratap, Shivaji and Guru Govind Singh as models; honouring those who died for the nation is part of the speech.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: His Calcutta 1939 presidential address (Hindu Rashtra Darshan), his economic policy of national co-ordination of class interests: he calls the attempt to interpret all human history and activity in economic terms alone one-sided, since man has other appetites and racial, cultural and national factors persist.

military-superiority.rationale: Keer's account of his writing has him arguing that national prosperity depends on discipline, gunpowder and military strength, and that just but weak states are smothered by strong ones; the 1941 and Mahasabha programme was Hindu militarisation.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Keer's biography (chapter 'Hindu Manifesto or Savarkarism', summarising his presidential addresses at Ahmedabad, Nagpur, Calcutta and Madura) reports: In the account of his 1937 address, Muslims are said to cherish secret designs to disintegrate the Indian State and create a state within a state; he singled out the Muslim minority as the only minority problem. This is his claim as reported, not independent evidence.

minority-language-support.rationale: In 1939 (Hindu Rashtra Darshan) and 1937 he promises that minorities' language, religion and culture will be expressly guaranteed, with separate schools in their own tongue and government help in proportion to the taxes they pay.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Keer quotes the Abhinav Bharat creed he led: the republic may be headed by a monarch or a president, which matters not much, so long as sovereign power rests with the Indian people; his leaflet to princes says the head of state, president or king, depends on how the revolution develops. Acceptance of a ceremonial monarch is implied, not stated, so low.

nation-first.rationale: Keer's biography (chapter 'Hindu Manifesto or Savarkarism', summarising his presidential addresses at Ahmedabad, Nagpur, Calcutta and Madura) reports: He held that Indian foreign policy should rest on serving, safeguarding and promoting the national self-interest, and that nations judge pacts by their own security and prosperity.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: In 1939 he says the Mahasabha will expressly guarantee minorities' rights in religion, culture and language: every minority may have separate schools teaching in its own tongue and its own religious and cultural institutions, receiving government help in proportion to the taxes it pays, on condition the majority's equal rights are not encroached. This is cultural institutions with state aid, not self-government as such, so medium.

national-mission.rationale: Keer's biography (chapter 'Hindu Manifesto or Savarkarism', summarising his presidential addresses at Ahmedabad, Nagpur, Calcutta and Madura) reports: On foreign policy he held it inadvisable to dictate to other countries to choose a particular form of government and said democracy itself demands that peoples choose their own.

national-rebirth.rationale: In 1937 he calls for the all-round regeneration of the Hindu people, telling Hindus that if they are up and doing all that is lost may yet be regained, and Keer says he believes in the resurrection of the Hindus. He ties it to consolidation and independence, not to a break with the past, so the term radical is not his, hence medium.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Keer says he was not a believer in mechanical orthodox socialism, rejected economic interpretations of all history, and styled his own policy nationalistic economy with national co-ordination of class interests, while saying the evils of capitalism lie in distribution and greed. He did not state the claim in these words, so low.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: He criticised absolute non-violence as perverse (My Transportation for Life, on Gandhi's movement), and per Keer wrote the play Sanyasta Khadga arguing that absolute non-violence fails and the sword protects homes.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: His 1948 statement says he led the movement against the vivisection of India and that the ambition to restore the integrity of the Motherland from the Indus to the Seas was not renounced. The sources are about partition, not a peace agreement, so this is medium.

open-borders.rationale: Keer's biography (chapter 'Hindu Manifesto or Savarkarism', summarising his presidential addresses at Ahmedabad, Nagpur, Calcutta and Madura) reports: He wrote that the earth is our motherland and a Human State the ultimate political goal, but warned nationalism cannot be abandoned while others keep their national bonds, so the position is only a distant ideal.

opposition-only-legal-channels.rationale: His 1948 statement calls the revolutionary mentality inevitable and justifiable while struggling against alien armed oppression, with a constitutional mentality only once the state is free; Keer's rule 'revolution outside, constitution within' says the same. His own record includes the Abhinav Bharat secret society.

patriotic-education.rationale: In the introduction to Six Glorious Epochs he says English-written histories taught in Indian schools falsely portray India as always conquered and that refuting them, for national honour and historical truth, is a national duty. That implies schooling should foster national pride but is not an explicit rule on patriotic teaching, so low.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: He opposed guaranteed community shares: in 1937 he demands one man one vote with no special weightage of representation for any community and no price paid for loyalty, and in 1948 he says the Mahasabha opposed the Communal Award. Those texts concern legislative seats, not executive power as such, so medium.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Six Glorious Epochs and the 1937 address defend Hindu cultural heritage and history against foreign deprecation, and the Mahasabha's mission is to preserve Hindu religious, racial and cultural identity.

promote-democracy-abroad.rationale: Keer's biography (chapter 'Hindu Manifesto or Savarkarism', summarising his presidential addresses at Ahmedabad, Nagpur, Calcutta and Madura) reports: He held that no form of government or political ism is good for all peoples alike, called empty slogans of democracy no guide to India's foreign policy, and held it inadvisable to dictate forms of government to others.

property-franchise.rationale: His 1937 presidential address demands one man one vote as the general rule irrespective of caste, creed, race or religion in the Indian State; nothing in his programme ties the vote to property.

property-fundamental.rationale: His Calcutta 1939 presidential address (Hindu Rashtra Darshan), his economic policy of national co-ordination of class interests: private property must in general be held inviolate, with no expropriation without reasonable recompense; but the Government may take over land for State cultivation in some cases and nationalise key industries, so it is a strong but not absolute right.

public-ownership.rationale: His Calcutta 1939 presidential address (Hindu Rashtra Darshan), his economic policy of national co-ordination of class interests: key industries or manufactures may be altogether nationalised if the National Government can afford to do so and can run them more efficiently than private enterprise.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Keer's biography (chapter on his social revolution at Ratnagiri) reports that he launched and led a movement for purifying Marathi of Urdu, Persian and English words and substituting pure Marathi and Sanskrit-derived ones, and that the Maharashtra Literary Conference accepted the principle. Medium because it is a biographer's account of his record.

race-social-construct.rationale: In Hindutva he calls the human race single, says talk of separate races is provisional and relatively true and that barriers between races are artificial, yet in the same passage he claims the Hindus as a racial unit bound by common blood (jati). His words point both ways.

racial-franchise.rationale: His 1937 presidential address demands one man one vote irrespective of caste, creed, race or religion, and no distinctions of religion or race in the franchise; his 1948 statement repeats equal rights for every loyal citizen irrespective of religion, caste or creed.

racial-group-interests.rationale: In 1937 he argues no movement is condemnable for being sectional so long as it defends the just rights of a nation or community without infringing others', and he built the Hindu Sanghatan on that basis; Keer repeats that defensive communalism is as justified as nationalism. His group is the Hindu race and nation, not racial groups in general.

racial-pride.rationale: The 1937 address urges Hindus to drop their apologetic attitude and take pride as descendants of a mighty people and of Hindu heroes, speaking of the Hindu race.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: He proposes an Indian State with no distinctions of race or religion in franchise, public services, offices or taxation (1937), and Keer reports he fought legal and customary segregation of untouchables in schools, temples and dining at Ratnagiri. His writings on race and Hindu identity do not propose segregation laws.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Keer's biography (chapter on his rationalist writing) reports that he stands for science and asks Hindus to test ancient works against science, not treating the Vedas and Smritis as omniscient. Medium because it is a biographer's account quoting his essays.

rehabilitation.rationale: In My Transportation for Life (his Andaman memoir) he writes that prison labour should improve the prisoner, that education in prison should be more compulsory than hard labour, that the aim of punishment is to reclaim convicts as future citizens, and that prisons are penitentiaries, not places of torture. He also insists prison must not be easy, so this is a rehabilitation-first view with strict discipline.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Keer's account of his essays has him urging Hindus to test their ancient laws and learning on the touchstone of science and follow what serves the nation, treating the Vedas and Smritis as historical landmarks, not unchangeable works.

religion-from-peoples-character.rationale: In Hindutva and the 1937 address he makes a religion of Indian origin, rooted in the Indian Holyland, the mark of the Hindu nation, and says a Hindu may hold any indigenous system, while faiths whose holyland lies abroad bind their followers elsewhere. That favours religion rooted in the people's own land and history, though he does not state the principle in terms of character.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: In 1937 he says the Hindu Mahasabha takes its stand on no dogma, book or school of philosophy, whether pantheist, monotheist or atheist, and leaves theology to individual or group conscience; he also insists Sikhs, Jains and Buddhists are within Hindudom on equal terms. This is about the Mahasabha's own stance, not state law, so medium.

religious-nation.rationale: His 1937 address says the Hindu Mahasabha is not mainly a religious body and that Hindutva is wider than Hinduism, resting on common country, culture, language and history, and leaving dogma to individual conscience; but the Holyland requirement excludes Muslims and Christians, so religion still marks the boundary. The sources point both ways.

remove-other-ethnic-groups-from-country.rationale: In 1937 he proposes an Indian State where all citizens are equal irrespective of religion or race with one man one vote, and Keer's summary of his programme says none would be deprived of equal rights of free citizenship while discharging the common obligations. He calls Muslims a dangerous community to watch but proposes no removal.

resist-oppression-despite-death.rationale: Keer quotes his argument that revolt, bloodshed and revenge are justified instruments against oppression and that every oppressor has his avenger, and the 1937 address honours those who went to the gallows for freedom. His own record is armed revolutionary activity and a transportation sentence. His 1857 book calls the death of those who rise against oppression an act the blame for which lies with the injustice that provoked it.

restore-past-order.rationale: Keer reports that he stands for today and not the blind traditions of yesterday, wants a casteless modern Hindu society, science against superstition and the machine age, and treats the Vedas and Smritis as historical works; he also celebrates the Hindu past and Hindu revival, so the answer is moderate.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: His Calcutta 1939 presidential address (Hindu Rashtra Darshan), his economic policy of national co-ordination of class interests: strikes or lockouts that cripple national industry or weaken the nation's economy must be referred to State arbitration and, in serious cases, quelled.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Keer reports his view that no form of government or political ism is absolutely good or bad under all circumstances, and that foreign policy should rest on national self-interest, not isms or bookish theory. That is about foreign policy and forms of government, not policy generally, so low.

return-to-foraging.rationale: In My Transportation for Life, describing the Javra hunter-gatherers of the Andamans, he rejects the view that a life without civilisation is plain and contented (are they contented and happy? By no means) and says they struggle for food as hard as civilised people. It is an aside about one tribe, not a statement on humanity, so low.

return-to-pre-conversion-religion.rationale: In My Transportation for Life he campaigned for reconversion (Shuddhi) of Hindus who had been converted to Islam or Christianity, urging that converts be taken back by ritual and given Hindu names as a social and religious duty; Keer records he began the reconversion movement at Ratnagiri in 1926. He applies it to people of Hindu origin returning to Hinduism.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: After 1947 he states the unaccomplished mission is restoring the integrity of the Motherland from the Indus to the Seas (Written Statement, 1948); Keer's biography has a chapter titled the fight for Akhand Hindusthan.

right-to-secede.rationale: He insists Hindusthan must remain one and indivisible from Kashmir to Rameshwar and Sindh to Assam (1937), and the 1948 statement records that he led the Mahasabha in refusing the Cripps clause that allowed partition.

sacred-nation.rationale: He defines the Hindu nation by a common Fatherland and Holyland (pitribhumi and punyabhumi) and honours its martyrs and heroes across generations (1937 address; Hindutva), which treats the nation as a sacred continuing community, though he does not say in these terms that it gives members' lives lasting meaning.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Keer quotes him: the Smritis and the Vedas are loved as historical books and landmarks, not as omniscient and unchangeable works.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: His Calcutta 1939 presidential address (Hindu Rashtra Darshan), his economic policy of national co-ordination of class interests: the national economic strength must grow and the nation be made economically self-sufficient; foreign aid or capital is not discussed, so medium.

separate-church-state.rationale: In his 1948 written statement he says the Mahasabha maintained that the Indian State should be essentially a secular State, with every loyal citizen having equal rights and duties irrespective of religion, caste or creed; Keer describes a non-sectarian State. He also leads a Hindu nation movement and promised state aid to minority religious institutions, so low.

single-official-language.rationale: In 1937 he demands that one language and script, the one understood by the overwhelming majority, be the national language and script of the Indian State (Nagari and Hindi in Keer's summary of his programme), while guaranteeing minorities separate schools in their own tongue. He backs a single national language but not the suppression of others, so low.

small-step-social-reform.rationale: Keer's biography (chapter 'Hindu Manifesto or Savarkarism', summarising his presidential addresses at Ahmedabad, Nagpur, Calcutta and Madura) reports: The chapter calls him not an orthodox Hindu and sets out radical views on social regeneration and revolution (castelessness, secular marriage customs, science against superstition) rather than reform that respects established institutions.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Record: as Mahasabha president during the Second World War he ran a Hindu militarisation campaign urging Hindus to enlist in the army, navy and air force, which Keer says raised the Hindu share of the army sharply. His record is the opposite of urging soldiers to refuse to fight.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: In his 1948 statement he says the Mahasabha demanded repeal of the Arms Act and licences for arms sales and he himself led that movement, which opposes limiting arms to state forces.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Keer reports he wanted Hindusthan to keep a policy of neutrality towards all nations in respect of their internal affairs and their mutual relations, while treating nations helpful to the Hindu nation as friends and allies. That is neutrality in disputes, not an explicit refusal to join blocs, so low.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Keer's summary of his programme guarantees all citizens freedom of speech, conscience, worship and association, and his 1948 statement says any change of leadership, however desirable, should be effected by constitutional means alone; in 1941 he criticised reliance on repression under the Defence of India Act.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: His Calcutta 1939 presidential address (Hindu Rashtra Darshan), his economic policy of national co-ordination of class interests: every step must be taken by the State to protect national industries against foreign competition, and the nation made economically self-sufficient.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Per Keer, he stands for science in every department of life and holds science is not responsible for capitalism's evils or modern war, which come from distribution and greed. This is support for science, not a claim it solves most problems.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Keer's programme pairs the machine age and science-led progress with a consolidated, modernised Hindu nation, and in 1937 he calls for the regeneration of Hindu religious, racial and cultural identity; he also asks Hindus to test ancient works against science, so the ancestral values he wants revived are selective.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Keer's biography (chapter 'Hindu Manifesto or Savarkarism', summarising his presidential addresses at Ahmedabad, Nagpur, Calcutta and Madura) reports: He called aggressive nationalism immoral in human relations and said Hindus do not aim at usurping what belongs to others; the chapter also gives his programme as defensive consolidation.

total-state.rationale: Keer's summary of his programme has fundamental rights of speech, conscience, worship and association for all citizens, limited only for public peace and order or national emergency, private property held inviolate in general, and separate minority schools; alongside nationalised key industries and state arbitration of strikes. That is a strong state but not one directing every area of life.

troops-home-from-abroad.rationale: Keer reports that in his 1939-40 appeal he asked the British Government not to use Indian forces outside India proper and to guard the Western frontier with Hindu forces. This concerns Indian troops under British command, not a general rule about bases abroad, so low.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Six Glorious Epochs says India's history, unlike other nations', is a consistent and unbroken record and rejects the view that it is an unbroken chain of defeat; the 1937 address presents the Hindu nation's history as continuing since about 2000 BC.

uniformed-youth.rationale: In 1939 he makes compulsory military training in universities, colleges and schools one of three items of the Mahasabha's immediate programme (Hindu Rashtra Darshan). He did not call for uniformed drilled youth movements as such, so low.

workers-anti-imperialist-capitalist-alli.rationale: Keer's summary of his economic programme calls for national co-ordination of class interests, encouragement and recompense for national capital, and both capital and labour subordinated to the nation; it does not speak of an alliance against foreign domination in these terms, so low.

workers-nation.rationale: His Calcutta 1939 presidential address (Hindu Rashtra Darshan), his economic policy of national co-ordination of class interests: he says economic unity cannot dissolve religious, racial and national antagonisms and restricts the immediate economic programme to the advance of the Hindu nation, with labour and capital subordinated to national requirements.

notes: Where sources conflict: his 1937-42 addresses promise equal citizenship and minority safeguards, while the same texts and his Six Glorious Epochs describe Muslims as a hostile nation and argue Hindus should have retaliated against enemy women and destroyed mosques; each answer follows the text that speaks to that statement. His economic programme and several policy answers rest on Keer's 1950 biography (a partisan but contemporary account) and are medium at most; the primary texts used are Hindutva, the Mahasabha addresses (Hindu Rashtra Darshan), his Andaman memoir, Six Glorious Epochs and the 1857 book. He died in 1966, so statements on later technology or politics are null. The Wikipedia article was read for leads only.
